analysis.summary: Chris opened with a price objection to the $9,500 proposal. Lauren quickly negotiated down, offering concessions on price (ending at $6,500), a monthly rolling contract, and a pause clause, and Chris agreed to receive a revised contract. Lauren committed to sending the updated contract the same day.
analysis.next_steps: Lauren to send a revised contract today reflecting $6,500/month, monthly rolling term, and a pause clause; Lauren to confirm internal approval for the reduced price.
strengths: Stayed calm and responsive to the prospect's price objection.
Moved the negotiation forward and secured an agreement in principle and a clear next step.
Demonstrated flexibility on contract terms (monthly rolling and pause clause) which addressed the prospect's needs.
Promised timely follow-up by committing to send the revised contract the same day.
areas_for_improvement: Did not probe to understand the root cause of the price objection or the prospect's priorities (budget drivers, must-haves vs nice-to-haves).
Conceded large price reductions quickly without quantifying value or defending the original price.
Made final-sounding concessions (dropping to $6,500) before confirming internal approval from leadership.
Failed to differentiate the offering vs the unnamed competing agencies or ask what those proposals include.
Did not clarify operational details or potential consequences of the monthly rolling agreement and pause clause (e.g., minimum notice, scope during pauses).
action_items: Send revised contract today reflecting agreed $6,500/month, monthly rolling term, and a pause clause as discussed.
Immediately confirm with your director/finance that $6,500 is an approved rate and document any internal approvals or constraints.
Include a clear scope of work and any deliverables in the revised contract so scope isn't ambiguous when price was reduced.
Clarify terms of the pause clause (notice period, maximum pauses allowed, scope when paused) before sending final agreement.
Ask Chris to share the competitor proposals or key differences so you can document and, if needed, justify the pricing position.
objections_raised: Price is too expensive compared to expectation.
Prefer not to remove any scope to reduce price.
Want monthly rolling contract instead of six-month commitment.
Require a pause clause so they aren't charged for paused months.
